subject: paper:eakin-2004
quote: married adults with ADHD reported poorer overall marital adjustment on the Dyadic Adjustment Scale (DAS; Spanier, 1989) and more family dysfunction on the Family Assessment Device (FAD; Eptein, Baldwin, & Bishop, 1983) than control adults.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). Standardised-measure evidence that adults with ADHD have poorer marital and family functioning than controls.

subject: paper:wymbs-2008
quote: parents of youths diagnosed with ADHD in childhood (n = 282) were more likely to divorce and had a shorter latency to divorce compared with parents of children without ADHD (n = 206).
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Higher divorce rate and shorter time-to-divorce among parents of youths with ADHD — the family-strain route, distinct from an adult partner's own ADHD.

subject: paper:bruner-2015
quote: Participants who reported clinically significant levels of both hyperactivity-impulsivity and inattentiveness (consistent with ADHD-C) had lower relationship quality than those whose self-reported symptoms indicated no ADHD diagnosis.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Young-adult evidence that ADHD symptom level tracks lower romantic relationship quality.

subject: paper:bruner-2015
quote: Emotion regulation problems and hostile relationship conflict mediated this association.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Identifies emotion-regulation problems and conflict as mediators of the ADHD-to-relationship-quality link, tying it to the emotional-dysregulation axis.

subject: paper:wymbs-2021
quote: much research points toward adults with attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) having short-lived and discordant romantic relationships
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). A 2021 review's summary of the converging literature — the relationships of adults with ADHD are shorter-lived and more discordant — giving the couple-strain finding review-level weight beyond the individual studies.

subject: paper:canu-2014
quote: Analyses revealed greater negativity and less positivity in C-couples' behavior during a conflict resolution task, relative to IA and ND couples, and this corresponded with couples' relational satisfaction.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Directly coded conflict behaviour: combined-type (C) couples were more negative and less positive than inattentive (IA) and non-diagnosed (ND) couples, and this tracked satisfaction — locating the observable conflict signature in the combined presentation.

subject: paper:canu-2014
quote: IA-couples emitted relational behavior that was largely similar to ND couples.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Inattentive-type couples behaved much like non-diagnosed couples on the coded task — the contrast that pins the conflict effect to the hyperactive-impulsive/combined phenotype rather than inattention.

subject: paper:bijlenga-2018
quote: We found that 39% of the male and 43% of the female ADHD patients had symptoms of a sexual dysfunction, and 17% of the male and 5% of the female ADHD patients had symptoms of any other sexual disorder.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). Clinic-sample prevalence of sexual dysfunction well above general-population rates in both sexes — an intimacy strand of relationship impairment distinct from conflict.

subject: paper:bijlenga-2018
quote: sexual dysfunctions and other sexual disorders are highly prevalent in adults with ADHD. Screening for sexual disorders should be therefore standard procedure during diagnostic assessment.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. The authors' conclusion and clinical recommendation — high prevalence plus a call to screen sexual functioning during ADHD assessment, given how rarely it had been diagnosed.

subject: paper:sacchetti-2017
quote: Higher levels of ADHD symptomology in college students were related to increased social impairment and higher levels of state and trait anger, but not romantic relationship satisfaction or rates of IPV.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Supports the emotional-dysregulation route (ADHD symptomology tracks state/trait anger and social impairment) while itself finding no association with romantic-relationship satisfaction or IPV — the null half feeds tension:adhd-relationship-effect-not-universal.
